title: Prepare an authorized Network Analyzer lab
summary: Review and preview the public interface first, then restrict any privileged wireless exercise to isolated hardware and a network you own or have written permission to test.
steps: Create an isolated lab with a compatible Linux system, a dedicated wireless adapter, and an access point you own or are authorized to test.
Clone the repository and inspect mybash.sh before granting it root privileges; review every external utility and operation it can invoke.
Use python3 server.py to preview the local interface at http://0.0.0.0:8000 without beginning a wireless assessment.
Install Aircrack-ng and mdk tooling from your distribution's trusted package repository and confirm the adapter supports the required lab mode.
Run the Bash workflow only inside the authorized lab. Do not capture third-party traffic, disrupt client connections, or audit credentials without explicit permission.
Remove captured material after the exercise and record the scope, authorization, date, device, and results.
command:
git clone https://github.com/Guang84/Network-Analyzer.git
cd Network-Analyzer
python3 server.py
# Review mybash.sh before any authorized lab-only execution
audience: Learners preparing an isolated, explicitly authorized wireless-security lab.
prerequisites: A compatible wireless adapter and access point you own or are authorized to test
Trusted distribution packages for Aircrack-ng and mdk tooling
verification: The local interface opens through the Python server
Required wireless utilities are detected from trusted package sources
The lab scope, devices, authorization, and time window are documented before privileged testing
troubleshooting: If the interface does not load, confirm the local server is running and port 8000 is available.
If wireless functions are unavailable, verify adapter support and the required Linux permissions before changing any network mode.
If a step could affect a third-party network or client, stop and re-check the authorization boundary.
